mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as long as the rate remains below 2.5%.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS decline below 2.5% fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger equity demand for defensive assets, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE increase > 0.5pp fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in manufacturing output (INDPRO) and employment growth (PAYEMS) indicate accelerating labor market contraction, causing negative equity returns over 20 days due to reduced corporate earnings visibility.
failure_condition: Joint decline in INDPRO and PAYEMS fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized), a decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) triggers equity sell-offs due to profit margin pressure, generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS decline in CPIAUCSL > 3.0 periods fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust manufacturing activity that elevates corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO increase fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) falling below 900 thousand units in the prior month indicate weakening residential demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days due to sector-specific equity repricing.
failure_condition: HOUST < 900.0 fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In low-interest-rate regimes (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%), a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals economic vulnerability that forces equity portfolio reallocation toward bonds, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.0% in FEDFUNDS < 2.5% periods fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP growth (GDPC1) indicate broad-based economic weakness that triggers negative equity returns over 60 days due to prolonged earnings recession.
failure_condition: Joint decline in HOUST and GDPC1 fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
